evidence_sources.rationale: spells/invoke/plan.md is the current normative Plan mode contract for purpose, composability, gates, execution entry, readiness, validation, ownership, and authority limits.
spells/invoke/README.md supplies the current Invoke ownership chain, upstream Design evidence requirements, capability-axis separation, and downstream handoff limits.
spells/invoke/PLAN-ARTIFACT-BOUNDARIES.md is the current source for artifact ownership, source-truth roles, hierarchy, ordering, disagreement, navigation, and execution-readiness rules.

The current retired-template declaration confirms that the historical implementation-plan surface is scaffolding and that Work Pack plus Implementation Layering now own executable planning and governance.
The current Implementation Layering template defines the L0-L3 decision, deferral, evidence, promotion, and non-regression semantics.

The current Work Pack template defines executable-plan source truth, internal planning units, validation, exact unit selection, execution-entry policy, closeout synchronization, gates, and authority ceilings.
The current Execution Pack template confirms the medium/high-complexity wave choreography role and its references to Work Pack, layering, tasks, and SWUs.

The completed prior implementation plan preserves domain evidence for objectives, delivery slices, ordered work, validation, failure behavior, and lifecycle handoff, but its executable claims are historical.
The prior layering artifact preserves concrete layer questions, minimum units, deferrals, exit evidence, promotion decisions, and non-regression semantics.
The prior Work Pack preserves concrete task, SWU, gate, blocker, validation, navigation, and execution-handoff concepts while its completion and readiness claims remain historical.
The prior Execution Pack preserves wave ordering, layer mapping, dependencies, parallelization, selection, and choreography semantics without current execution authority.
The prior validation artifact preserves the distinction between exact checks, evidence boundaries, structural closure, and runtime residue; its pass claims are historical.
The prior Distill result preserves atomicity, first-unit, recomposition, blocker, selection, escalation, and owner-boundary concepts while its verdict is historical.
The prior gap ledger preserves typed gap and blocker ownership, severity, repair route, and resolution semantics.
The prior Invoke result preserves separate authoring, structural validity, mutation-readiness, lifecycle-owner, and next-route meanings; its status claims are historical.
The thin successor context preserves the authoring-source, candidate-bundle, bundle-admission, and evidence-state semantic units but is not a current correctness oracle.
The thin closure receipt preserves historical independent-disposition and consumer-topology evidence; its readiness and authority claims are historical.
The thin Define source preserves explicit relations and boundaries for the evidence-bearing Plan successor layer, subject to current-contract reassessment.
The generated thin definitions preserve the four evidence-layer meanings, while generated status and authority claims are historical only.
The prior admission receipt preserves clean-replay, inventory, drift, consumer-validation, and authority-ceiling semantics but grants no current admission.
The expanded successor context supplies the candidate semantic denominator for Plan subject, parts, validity, handoff, and evidence state, with every unit reassessed against current sources.
The expanded closure receipt preserves independently assessed dispositions and the catalogued consumer topology while its executable outcome remains historical.

The expanded Define source supplies the explicit eighteen-unit candidate inventory and its historical relation and boundary denominator; current evidence requires relation corrections and two additional independent execution-boundary units.

facets.rationale: Invoke Plan is represented as the governed, non-mutating conversion of one approved Design into executable planning artifacts and a bounded handoff.

The model independently retains Work Pack, Implementation Layering, delivery slices, layers, waves, tasks, SWUs, implementation-detail contracts, validation obligations, gates, blockers, gaps, execution entry, closeout synchronization, and Execution Pack.

Direct relations encode source-truth references, governed-child dependencies, independent wave ordering of tasks and SWUs, exact selection, validation feeds, and choreography contrast without relying on indirect or reciprocal substitutes.
Authored, bundled, admitted, readiness-proved, accepted, and execution-authorized states remain separate and require current evidence owned by the responsible producer or validator.
Validation obligations, Plan gates, Distill outcomes, artifact agreement, readiness preflight, blocker escalation, and evidence-timing rules are independently materialized.

The model covers exact unit selection, finite route projection, Task Session handoff, mutation stop decisions, one-SWU execution boundaries, terminal closeout synchronization, and choreography without claiming execution.

Approved Design is bound as upstream authority; Invoke owns planning contracts only, while acceptance, mutation, target lifecycle work, promotion, publication, deployment, and runtime receipts remain with their declared downstream owners.

includes: The sole authored machine-readable source for one Plan generation, including Work Pack semantics, requested effect, finite frontier, routes, write scopes, budgets, validation contracts, and readiness configuration.
excludes: Separately authored WPRA configuration or human Work Pack views, generated files, derived IDs or digests, producer and validator decisions, owner acceptance, execution receipts, and execution authority.
conditions: It must bind the exact admitted Design predecessor it consumes and must be the only semantic input from which deterministic Plan artifacts are generated.

includes: Every required generated Plan artifact and the exact producer receipt for one deterministic generation, including the Work Pack, Implementation Layering, execution-entry projection, and required companion views.
excludes: Independent bundle admission, implementation readiness as execution admission, owner acceptance, task execution, product mutation, promotion, publication, and deployment.
conditions: Every member must derive from the same exact Plan execution source and producer run, and deterministic rehearsals must agree before the candidate can advance.

includes: Independent clean replay, exact inventory comparison, predecessor freshness, structural validation, semantic projection checks, and declared consumer results for one exact Plan candidate bundle.
excludes: Semantic invention, Design revision, implementation readiness, owner acceptance, execution authorization, target lifecycle completion, and product mutation.
conditions: Admission is point-in-time evidence and must be produced by an executable identity independent from the candidate-bundle producer.

includes: Separate authored, admitted, readiness-proved, owner-accepted, and execution-authorized axes with exact current receipt references and evidence ceilings.
excludes: A collapsed generic PASS, inferred readiness, planned validators or fixtures represented as executed evidence, inferred acceptance, and inferred mutation permission.
conditions: Every positive axis must be supported by byte-current evidence owned by the producer, validator, decision owner, or runtime owner responsible for that axis.
A Plan readiness preflight is acceptance-critical compatibility evidence but remains non-reusable for execution, non-mutation-ready, and authority-free.

includes: The governed, non-mutating translation of one approved Design into an implementation objective, canonical Work Pack, global Implementation Layering, ordered executable units, validation, gates, blockers, gaps, and an exact execution handoff boundary.
excludes: Reopening approved product or architecture discovery, silently editing upstream Design, executing tasks or SWUs, mutating product source, accepting product changes, promoting definitions, completing a spell or sigil lifecycle, publishing, releasing, or deploying.
conditions: Normal planning requires approved and stable Design evidence, explicit source references and delivery boundary, one global Implementation Layering source of truth, one Work Pack source of truth, a validation strategy, and no unresolved acceptance-critical blocker.

Medium and high complexity require split task and wave contracts, implementation-detail contracts, SWUs, layer-mapped waves, and an Execution Pack; missing required companions or acceptance-critical detail blocks or escalates to the named decision owner.

Plan must stop at the downstream owner boundary and name Task Session, Spellcraft, Sigil Development, Implementation Readiness, Decision Gate, or a deferred route without claiming that owner's result.

includes: The source of truth for executable planning and current execution readiness: objective, delivery slices, task and SWU manifests, validation strategy, blockers, gaps, gate status, output mode, active layer window, current state, execution policy, navigation, and exact closeout contracts.
excludes: Layer philosophy and promotion authority owned by Implementation Layering, duplicated deep task-local detail owned by useful split task contracts, and cross-task choreography owned by the Execution Pack.
conditions: If the Work Pack, wave contracts, and task contracts disagree, the Work Pack gate must be block until reconciliation.
Task-board, wave, SWU, parent-task, and source-contract references must be navigable when their targets exist.
Low complexity may remain reviewable and single-file; scope beyond the low-complexity limits must use split output.

Mutation-capable execution requires a passing Work Pack gate, complete exact frontier, current route and validation digests, complete closeout synchronization, and the required non-reusable readiness proof.

includes: The single global source of truth and governance lens for L0-L3 decision boundaries, layer questions, minimum working units, included and deferred scope, exit evidence, promotion decisions, nested layer policy, and non-regression guarantees.
excludes: Task execution instructions, task or SWU status tracking, source-of-truth task contracts, execution choreography, and mutation authority.
conditions: Every Plan has exactly one global Implementation Layering artifact.
Later layers must preserve guarantees proven by earlier layers, deferred scope must remain explicit, and promotion must cite evidence from the previous layer rather than preference.

includes: One coherent delivered outcome, its included boundary, dependencies, layer and wave mapping, and the validation evidence by which that outcome is accepted.
excludes: Execution ordering, task-local implementation instructions, SWU atomicity, and independent mutation authority.
conditions: Every delivery slice must map to one or more Plan tasks and must have an explicit validation strategy.

includes: One L0-L3 decision boundary with its question, minimum working unit, included scope, explicit deferrals, exit evidence, promotion decision, and preserved earlier guarantees.
excludes: Task implementation detail, execution status, preference-only promotion, and silently imported later-layer scope.
conditions: The layer must state what will be known after completion, and advancement beyond it must cite its current exit evidence and the required evidence from the preceding layer.

includes: The execution-order surface for a layer-aligned group of tasks and SWUs, including wave goal, layer question, dependencies, entry gate, included units, parallelization boundaries, local status, exit evidence, and promotion evidence.
excludes: Detailed algorithms, source-of-truth task or SWU definitions, unrelated global Plan rationale, and independent execution authority.
conditions: Each wave must name its implementation layer, layer question, promotion evidence, and exit gate.
Wave order must agree with task and SWU dependencies.
Parallel units must have disjoint write scopes or an explicit merge plan.

includes: One implementation responsibility with objective, parent slice and layer, one-or-more wave memberships, source contracts, dependencies, blocker state, write scope, SWUs or a valid exemption, done criteria, validation, handoff, synchronization, completion evidence, and task-local status.
excludes: Global Plan rationale, unrelated task state, vague outcome-only instructions, actual implementation work, and authority outside the task's declared scope.
conditions: A split task file must be a useful executable contract rather than a title placeholder.
Medium and high complexity execution tasks must carry implementation detail and decompose into SWUs unless they satisfy the exact closure-only exemption.
A task description that only names a bundle, layer, component, or outcome blocks or flags until concrete implementation detail is supplied.

includes: The smallest independently executable and reviewable implementation step, with exactly one primary behavior or decision, exactly one parent task, an independently reviewable acceptance boundary, split analysis, dependencies, explicit write scope, source anchors, related context, done criteria, acceptance evidence, validation, execution-owner recommendation, and handoff context.
excludes: Multiple independently verifiable behaviors bundled for convenience, task-shaped combinations of structure, responsive behavior, projection, interaction, or separate workspace regions, pre-generated runtime context packs, and execution performed by Plan.
conditions: Every SWU belongs to exactly one task and must also carry its direct wave and implementation-layer ordering dependencies.
If plausible child units can pass independently, the SWU must be split.
The first selected SWU must be the narrowest reversible trust-building step.
Missing dependencies, source context, write scope, done criteria, acceptance evidence, validation, execution owner, or handoff context blocks mutation-capable handoff.

includes: The task-level purpose and decision, inputs, outputs, data model or state, interfaces, data flow, ordered algorithm or pseudocode, precedence or transition rules, edge cases, failure modes, constraints, acceptance checks, and validation evidence needed for safe execution.
excludes: New product or architecture decisions owned by Design, unrelated implementation choices, placeholder task labels, and reopening product discovery during execution.
conditions: It is required for medium and high complexity execution tasks and for any task whose domain logic, ranking, scoring, classification, policy, transition, parsing, reconciliation, optimization, or transformation cannot be executed from a title alone.
Acceptance-critical missing detail blocks Plan handoff or escalates through the named decision route; non-critical detail may remain only as an owned Plan gap with a repair path.

includes: One exact runnable command or reviewable check with a named target, pre-execution, post-produce, or closeout timing, expected result, evidence output, acceptance effect, and failure owner.
excludes: Unrunnable aspirations, future outputs represented as current PASS, and a requirement that a declared post-produce output or validator exist before its producing SWU runs.
conditions: Every delivery slice and every non-exempt SWU must have validation evidence.
The validation phase must match when the required artifact can exist.
Failed acceptance-critical validation blocks the affected gate, selection, or handoff.

includes: A typed evidence condition controlling advancement of a layer, wave, task, selected unit, Work Pack, or execution handoff, with named target, required evidence, accepted outcomes, current decision, and blocker causes.
excludes: Implicit approval, generic PASS without typed target evidence, planned fixtures or validators treated as executed proof, owner acceptance, mutation admission, promotion, publication, or deployment.
conditions: Missing approved Design evidence, required source references, required companions, validation strategy, implementation detail, SWU contract fields, closeout synchronization, or artifact agreement blocks the affected transition.
A Distill flag may advance only with every gap, owner, and repair path recorded; a Distill block prevents mutation-capable routing, and mutation-capable handoff requires the required Distill pass.

An execution-candidate requires the exact final Work Pack readiness audit and Implementation Readiness preflight over complete frontier routes and typed validation contracts, with a real proof-only TASK_READY guard result that remains non-reusable, non-mutation-ready, and authority-free.
A disagreement among Work Pack, wave, and task contracts, stale semantic or route digests, an unsafe or unknown route, or an unresolved acceptance-critical blocker keeps the gate blocked.
A positive gate decision must cite current evidence for the exact bound target.

includes: A known cause that prevents a named current claim or transition, including its affected boundary, dependencies, severity, owner, next action, and repair route.
excludes: Non-blocking future improvement, an unowned vague concern, and a gap that leaves the current bounded claim valid.
conditions: The blocker must stop the affected gate, selection, or handoff until repaired or explicitly resolved by its authorized owner.
A consequential unresolved semantic, scope, product, architecture, cost, risk, or protected-effect choice must escalate to the named decision owner rather than being guessed or silently deferred.

includes: A missing item or evidence residue with a non-blocking rationale, severity, owner, repair route, and explicit escalation condition.
excludes: Any condition that already prevents acceptance, current readiness, recomposition, required navigation, or safe execution.
conditions: The current bounded claim must remain valid without the missing item.
A flagged gap must name its owner and repair path.
The gap escalates to a Plan blocker when it becomes acceptance-critical, invalidates recomposition or navigation, changes semantic scope, or prevents safe execution.

includes: The exact selected execution unit, task and SWU identity, dependencies, finite frontier position, route, capability owner, target, write and effect scope, required inputs, typed validation contracts, current evidence, admission timing, entry state, next owner, expected receipt, and stop conditions handed from Plan.
excludes: Task or SWU execution, implicit successor selection, broader mutation authority, destructive or external effects, promotion, publication, deployment, reusable execution admission, and runtime context packs generated during planning.
conditions: The selector must reference exactly one applicable execution unit; when a task contains multiple SWUs, exactly one SWU must be selected before mutation-capable work begins.

New plans default to selected-unit-at-task-session: expected unmaterialized selection evidence is selection-ready rather than a refresh defect, and selection-ready must route to Implementation Readiness rather than directly to Task Session.
Exactly one truthful entry state and a consistent next owner are permitted.

The selected route must be one of the exact digest-bound allowed routes for the selected frontier unit and must retain its exact capability, mode, target, write scope, effect class, inputs, validation contract, and expected receipt.

Automatic decisions are limited to declared internal routing, reversible local defaults, declared fallback, one same-route retry after REPAIRABLE_OWNER_CONDITION, and fresh resumption where permitted.

Plan must stop for product or semantic choice, scope expansion, destructive or irreversible effects, credentials or secrets, external messaging or network effects, cost or risk acceptance, authority promotion, publication, deployment, or failed acceptance-critical validation.
Unknown effects or decisions, stale route digests, unsafe paths, unknown frontier references, contradictory state, missing closeout contracts, or failed entry validation block before mutation.
A pre-execution owner prerequisite for an already resolved Task Session attempt must return to that same attempt and resume context building exactly once; it must not start a second Task Session.

includes: The predeclared terminal source receipt contract, exact synchronization target inventory, baseline binding, admitted delta classes, lifecycle-owner route and validation, expected owner receipt, exact-write evidence, continuity evidence, and deterministic successor policy for one mutation-capable SWU.
excludes: Implementation admission, another SWU, inferred or unrelated targets, authority change, promotion, publication, deployment, destructive cleanup, policy or cost-risk acceptance, and source targets discovered only after mutation.
conditions: Every mutation-capable SWU must have exactly one complete closeout synchronization contract before Task Session admission.
Missing target inventory, baseline binding, admitted deltas, owner validation, expected receipt, or a unique dependency-ready successor-or-none policy blocks handoff before source mutation.
The closeout route is limited to the exact declared planning and evidence targets and may not widen implementation or authority scope.

includes: The medium/high-complexity cross-task choreography view for wave order, stage coverage, dependencies, closure obligations, SWU scheduling, entry and exit evidence, and parallelization boundaries.
excludes: Work Pack source truth, source-of-truth task specifications, source-of-truth SWU definitions, independent execution state, implementation algorithms, and mutation authority.
conditions: Every referenced wave, task, SWU, dependency, layer assignment, and status must agree with the Work Pack graph.
Medium and high complexity require an Execution Pack or an explicit blocking record.
It may schedule and present Work Pack units but must not redefine them.
